articles.title: ‘I will be the fielding coach’: Ex-England captain's dig at India as BCCI invites applications
articles.summary: Former England captain Michael Vaughan took a cheeky dig at India's catching woes after the BCCI invited applications for the position of fielding coach
articles.body: Former England captain Michael Vaughan took a cheeky dig at India's catching woes after the BCCI invited applications for the position of fielding coach for the Senior Women's National Team.Reacting to the announcement on X, Vaughan wrote: "I will be the fielding coach."The BCCI has set November 16 as the deadline for applications for the fielding coach's position, along with that of head physiotherapist for the Senior Men's National Team.Vaughan's remark comes at a time when India's fielding standards have been under scrutiny following a series of costly lapses. The team's catching problems were particularly evident during the Women's T20 World Cup 2026, where India dropped 10 catches across five group-stage matches.Three of those dropped chances came against South Africa, with Marizanne Kapp making India pay after receiving multiple lifelines. India eventually suffered a group-stage exit, with their fielding attracting widespread criticism.Head coach Amol Muzumdar had acknowledged the shortcomings, admitting that the team needed to improve across all three departments, including batting, bowling and fielding.However, the problem has continued beyond the global tournament. India dropped four catches during their three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe before missing another four opportunities in the opening ODI of the subsequent series.Wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh was among those to struggle, dropping two catches, including a regulation opportunity behind the stumps. Deepti Sharma and Kranti Gaud also missed chances, while India failed to convert a couple of run-out opportunities.Although India completed a 3-0 sweep in the ODI series, the repeated fielding errors have raised questions about the team's efforts to address the issue.The BCCI has laid down specific eligibility criteria for the fielding coach's role. Applicants must have either represented India or another country at the international level, hold a minimum BCCI Level 'B' coaching certification or an equivalent qualification along with at least 30 first-class matches, or have coached an international team for one season or a T20 franchise or state team for at least two seasons.India's next assignment will be an all-format tour of South Africa in December. The teams will play a one-off Test in Gqeberha from December 9, followed by three ODIs from December 16 and three T20Is from December 26.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: India won the toss and elected to field first in the opening ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday.
articles.body: India won the toss and elected to field first in the opening ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. Captain Shubman Gill confirmed that India have opted for a pace-heavy attack, going in with four fast bowlers and two all-rounders.Mohammed Siraj and Kuldeep Yadav have missed out on the playing XI as India look to exploit the conditions in Auckland. Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Arshdeep Singh and Naman Dhir are among the players featuring in India's combination, with Axar Patel providing the second all-round option.Explaining his decision at the toss, Gill said: "We're going to bowl first. A little bit of overcast, if there's any reduction in the overs, it's always good to have a target on the board."Gill also highlighted the importance of the series in India's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa."Extremely important, I'd say. The conditions that we are going to get here would be a lot more similar to the ones in South Africa as compared to other parts of the world. So in terms of that, it'll be a really good experience for us," he said.New Zealand, meanwhile, have made a change at the top of the order, with Tim Seifert coming in for Devon Conway, who is recovering from a head knock sustained during training.Captain Mitchell Santner confirmed that Conway was making progress but would sit out the opening encounter."Conway's doing well. Obviously a bit of a head knock yesterday. So he's just going to rest up and he's obviously not playing today," Santner said.Seifert will open alongside Will Young, while Henry Nicholls completes New Zealand's top three.Santner also pointed to the opportunities created by squad rotation amid a demanding international schedule."With the schedules in both teams, it's been a little bit more rotation than probably would be usually. articles.title: 'We learned some great lessons': McCullum reflects on Pakistan setback ahead of Australia challenge
articles.summary: England head coach Brendon McCullum is hoping his team can turn the disappointment of their recent ODI tri-series campaign in Pakistan into valuable
articles.body: England head coach Brendon McCullum is hoping his team can turn the disappointment of their recent ODI tri-series campaign in Pakistan into valuable lessons as they prepare for a challenging white-ball tour of Australia.England arrived in Perth on Monday for an eight-match assignment against Australia, featuring three ODIs and five T20Is. The series gets underway on November 13 and will serve as an important part of their preparations for next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, according to the ICC website.The tour also marks England's return to Australia following their disappointing Ashes campaign earlier this year. However, McCullum is keen to look forward rather than dwell on the past, viewing the upcoming contests as an opportunity to assess his team's progress and methods."Firstly, it's nice to be back. An Australia tour is always a great tour. The cricket's always pretty competitive. We'll play at some great stadiums, against a good side, and continue to test our methods, towards the one-day World Cup," McCullum said.The England coach also stressed the importance of maintaining an aggressive approach while using the demanding schedule to improve the players' fitness."We know we need to keep getting better, but we've been presented with some good opportunities, and this will be one of those in the next couple of weeks. We want to play a high-octane, robust style of play, which demands fitness elements to it. So for us, this is a great opportunity to have a little fitness block in and around the demand of this series," he added.McCullum keen to build on Pakistan tri-series experienceEngland had a mixed outing in the ODI tri-series in Pakistan, where they managed only one win across four matches and failed to secure a place in the final.There were, however, encouraging individual performances. Captain Harry Brook and opener Ben Duckett impressed with the bat, while Liam Dawson, Sonny Baker and Jamie Overton contributed with the ball.Despite falling short of their target, McCullum believes the tournament offered important exposure, particularly for a relatively inexperienced squad that needs more time in one-day cricket.Reflecting on the campaign, he admitted that the result was disappointing but highlighted the benefits of facing different opponents, adapting to varying conditions and dealing with different tactical challenges."It was disappointing. Obviously, it was great to play in the tri-series. With the view towards the World Cup, the ability to be able to bounce between games, and different tactics, and different oppositions was good," McCullum said."We obviously didn't quite achieve what we wanted to, but we played some really good cricket and learned some great lessons. They should hold you in good stead in 12 months. We've got a pretty inexperienced team. These guys haven't played a lot of one-day cricket, so any opportunity to get experience and education, and those pressure moments, so that you can start to just understand a little bit better, it's going to be good," he added.The 2027 World Cup will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, giving England a year to strengthen their preparations and build a settled combination.England squads for Australia tourODI squad: Harry Brook (c), Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Tom Banton, Jacob Bethell, Jordan Cox, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Ben Duckett, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Joe Root, Josh Tongue.T20I squad: Harry Brook (c), Tom Banton, Jacob Bethell, James Coles, Jordan Cox, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Aneurin Donald, Eddie Jack, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Thomas Rew, Phil Salt, Luke Wood.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: There is no home advantage anymore: Michael Bracewell
articles.summary: MUMBAI: New Zealand may have lost the T20I series 3-2 but victories in the final two matches have boosted their belief ahead of the five-match ODI series
articles.body: MUMBAI: New Zealand may have lost the T20I series 3-2 but victories in the final two matches have boosted their belief ahead of the five-match ODI series against India, which begins at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. Calling India and New Zealand evenly matched sides, New Zealand allrounder Michael Bracewell expects another fiercely-contested series."I think it's two really evenly matched teams. We had a great ODI series in India at the start of the year and were able to win that series 2-1. India will remember that series and want to right some wrongs. Whenever two top teams face each other, it's always going to be a tough battle."We're certainly not taking India lightly. They're a great side and have match-winners all over the park," Bracewell said during a virtual media interaction. The 35-year-old dismissed the notion that New Zealand would start as favourites simply because they are playing at home. "We like playing in our own conditions and are used to playing here in New Zealand. But international cricket now means everyone travels and plays around the world so much that home advantage is probably not as significant as it once was. We're excited for a great series.," he said.(Watch the India-New Zealand ODI series, starting November 4 from 7.30 am IST, live on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ayush Doseja was getting a bit anxious after a string of low scores in the first three matches of the Ranji Trophy season.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ayush Doseja was getting a bit anxious after a string of low scores in the first three matches of the Ranji Trophy season. After a stellar debut season of 949 runs last year, his meagre returns this season could have pushed him back in the pecking order of India’s targeted players. On Tuesday, he maintained his composure to bail Delhi out of a tricky situation on the second day of their Ranji Trophy match against Services at the Air Force Ground in Palam.Delhi were delicately placed at 135/5 in reply to Services’ first-innings score of 266 when Doseja was joined by Delhi’s new crisis man, Sumit Mathur. The two southpaws stitched together a partnership of 144 runs before Doseja fell, caught down the leg side, for a patient 78. Delhi went to stumps at 299/6, with Mathur batting on 80 and Dev Lakra at the other end.The pitch here at Palam offered slow turn. Scoring freely was difficult, but Doseja found the right tempo. He said he had to cut out the extravagant shots to ensure he batted long. “I needed to ensure I didn’t play any rash shot. We had to secure the first-innings lead. There were murmurs around me about my form but I tried to cut them out,” said Doseja, who was put on the BCCI’s list of targeted players. “The time spent with Wasim Jaffer and Hrishikesh Kanitkar at the CoE has helped me understand my game better. There are 92 pitches at the CoE, which prepares us to play on any surface,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India face tricky Eden Park: Gill leads full-strength ODI side; Conway concussion hits NZ
articles.summary: Batting stars Shubman Gill, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul are back in the mix, while Mohammed Siraj is set to strengthen the pace attack.
articles.body: Batting stars Shubman Gill, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul are back in the mix, while Mohammed Siraj is set to strengthen the pace attack. Their first challenge in th first ODI against New Zealand on Wednesday, though, will be to figure out a ground where the boundaries can be as misleading as the bounce on offer.Eden Park is not your typical cricket ground. It is small, oddly shaped and has dimensions that can leave captains and bowlers scratching their heads. A shot that clears the rope comfortably in one direction might not travel nearly as far in another. For batters, that means knowing which side to target. For bowlers, it is about getting their lengths right and not allowing the short boundaries to dictate their plans.The short boundaries do tempt the batters into mindless slogging, but the pitch usually tells a much sterner story. Eden Park's drop-in tracks are lively and offer steep, tennis-ball bounce. In many ways, it serves as an early, unscripted dress rehearsal for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, where steep lift and seam movement is bound to test Indian techniques. Surviving isn't just about clearing the straight boundary, it's about riding the bounce and respecting the new ball."Ground dimensions is always one to play into your mind at Eden Park. Traditionally, there's a little bit of bounce, which, you know, is good for the seamers. And it can be quite swirly with the wind, which can make it quite a tough catching ground," New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said on Tuesday.The wind, in particular, could make life difficult for fielders, especially in the deep. And there is another factor that skipper Gill will be watching closely.The ODIs are scheduled to start at 3pm local time, later than what teams are accustomed to at this venue.Gill was candid about the unfamiliar conditions. "It is my first time that we are playing so late, we are playing at 3pm, so in the second innings, when we are bowling or batting, I don't know what the conditions will be like, and when you play with two new balls, at night it is possible that there is more swing, more bounce, more seam, and that will be very interesting," the India captain said.India's team combination will look considerably different from the one that featured in the T20I series. Rohit and Gill are bound to open, with Kohli, Shreyas Iyer and KL Rahul giving the middle order considerable experience. The presence of these senior players also means India can afford to approach the innings differently, without having to chase the high-risk template of T20 cricket.The bowling combination will be worth watching. Siraj's experience and Arshdeep Singh's ability to generate swing could give India a useful pace combination. How they fit in the two spinners, likely to be Axar Patel and Kuldeep Yadav, will depend on the surface and the balance they want in the XI.Conway suffers concussionNew Zealand, meanwhile, have had little luck leading up to the series opener. Mark Chapman and Rachin Ravindra were already ruled out of the series and Devon Conway on Tuesday joined them on the sidelines after suffering a concussion during training.Conway's absence is another blow to the hosts' batting plans, with Tim Seifert expected to step in. Skipper Santner will need the experienced trio of Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham and the in-form Glenn Phillips to shoulder more responsibility during the series if the Black Caps do not want to concede home ground.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: When the ball stops swinging, and pitches offer nothing off the surface, how do you trouble an international batter? For Shubman Gill, the formula is simple: sheer height, raw pace and steep bounce.On the eve of India’s opening ODI against New Zealand at the Eden Park, Auckland, the Indian skipper laid bare the blueprint behind India’s recent pace-bowling auditions, pegging tall, hit-the-deck quicks as a core priority with an eye on the 2027 World Cup in South Africa."When the ball gets old, when there is not much seam or swing movement, then how do you challenge the batter?" Gill said. "You can challenge the batter either if there is something in the wicket... or you can challenge the batter with pace and bounce."In recent times, several towering fast bowlers including Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana and newcomer Gurnoor Brar have represented India in the 50-over scheme of things. "Identifying the kind of bowlers that can make run-scoring difficult for the batters and that can give us the best opportunity to take wickets in the middle overs — that has been the thinking around trying someone like a Gurnoor or a Prasidh, which gives us a bit more than someone who is bowling at maybe 135 (kph) when the wicket is flat."I have played in the middle overs a lot, and I have seen that if those bowlers can hit the right areas — obviously hitting the right areas is the key — if tall fast bowlers can hit the right areas, it is a lot more difficult to score runs than someone who is bowling at 130-135. You have to be really precise with your shot-making. You have to be really on top of your game to be able to score against someone who is 140-plus and who is 6'1", 6'2", 6'3". There is a lot more risk when you are trying to score freely against that kind of bowler," Gill said.One big concern for India in the lead-up to the 2027 World Cup is the fitness of their key seam-bowling allrounder Hardik Pandya, who has been out of action since IPL 2026 thanks to a series of injuries and niggles.Calling Hardik's skill set difficult to replace, Gill said the team had remained in touch with him and hoped he would return to domestic cricket before making his comeback to the national side."Firstly, he is a great player," Gill stressed. "The qualities that he brings to the team, not many players in the world possess those qualities, to be able to have a fast-bowling allrounder who can bowl (in any phase) of the game, with the new ball, middle overs and death overs; and the kind of batting he has. Hopefully, we will see him back in the side soon."The captain, however, would have preferred a different arrangement for the New Zealand tour, with the ODI series sandwiched between the T20Is and two Tests. The tight turnaround means several members of the Test squad, including Gill, will miss the fourth and fifth ODIs. Jasprit Bumrah, meanwhile, has been rested for the entire ODI series.With the ODI World Cup and the World Test Championship final both scheduled for 2027, Gill felt India could have benefited from having their strongest available combinations for both formats in the ongoing tour."If it was in my hands and all the players were fit, I would have liked to have all the players we are looking at playing during the World Cup for the full ODI series. But the two Test matches are also very important," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India series 'taxing', players 'jarred' ahead of ODIs: Mitchell Santner
articles.summary: Modern international cricket rarely pauses to catch its breath, and New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner made no effort to sugarcoat the physical toll on
articles.body: Modern international cricket rarely pauses to catch its breath, and New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner made no effort to sugarcoat the physical toll on Tuesday.On the eve of the five-match ODI series opener against India at Eden Park, Auckland, Santner admitted the relentless, cross-format schedule has left his squad feeling "a little jarred" and deemed the packed home series decidedly "taxing".Across just over a month, the two sides are cramming in five T20Is across four venues followed by five ODIs and two high-stakes World Test Championship Tests starting November 19. For the two teams, the transition from breathless 20-over night fixtures to 50-over grinds has come with virtually zero breathing room."It's a very quick turnaround. With the travel and the late finishes in T20 cricket, the guys are a little bit jarred. Recovery is a massive part of modern-day cricketing schedule nowadays," Santner said. "With one-day cricket and quick turnarounds, it can be quite taxing. You want to play your best team all the time, but with the schedules these days and the quick turnarounds, it's pretty hard to do."The demanding schedule, complicated further by heavy dew and late-night travel during the T20 leg, has forced the Black Caps to rethink their match-eve routines. Long net sessions have taken a backseat to ice baths, physio rooms and active recovery."Guys just have to be on top of it. Whatever it looks like... So training might look like another recovery day rather than bowling a lot," Santner said.That squeeze makes player rotation inevitable — a necessity Santner believes comes with a silver lining. "...it creates depth, and we've seen guys coming in and stepping up straight away," he pointed out.Looming over this wear and tear is a ticking clock. With the 2027 ODI World Cup less than a year away, Santner acknowledged the tournament in South Africa could mark the final ODI chapter for several members of New Zealand's ageing squad, including himself."Everyone's kind of 34 or 35," said the 34-year-old Santner. "With one-day cricket being in the cycle after this World Cup, the focus is going to shift again to T20 cricket with the T20 World Cup being the next priority. So, yeah, I guess no one's told me anything yet, but it could be."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Indian cricket went through a dark phase’: Sachin Tendulkar's big revelation on captaincy stint
articles.summary: Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has offered an insight into his unsuccessful stints as India's captain, admitting that he did not always have complete
articles.body: Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has offered an insight into his unsuccessful stints as India's captain, admitting that he did not always have complete control over team selection during his leadership years in the 1990s.Tendulkar, who represented India across formats during an international career spanning 24 years, addressed the subject during an 'Ask Me Anything' session on Reddit on Tuesday. He also named his favourite Indian captains and shared his admiration for South Africa skipper Temba Bavuma.The batting great, who made his international debut on November 15, 1989, and retired on November 16, 2013, described leading India as a tremendous honour. However, he acknowledged that the role came with limitations, particularly when it came to choosing the playing XI."It was a great honour to lead the team as captain. However, I didn’t always have the freedom to pick my team entirely on my own. The BCCI today is a far more professional organisation than it was in the 1990s. Indian cricket also went through a particularly dark phase during that period," Tendulkar said.Despite his stature as one of the greatest batters in the history of the game, Tendulkar's two separate spells as India's captain in the 1990s did not produce the desired results.Tendulkar names Ganguly and Dhoni as favourite captainsWhen asked about his preferred leaders, the former India captain picked Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni, both of whom played significant roles in shaping Indian cricket."As far as my favourite captains go, Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni would definitely be at the top of my list!!," Tendulkar said.Both captains shared memorable World Cup moments with Tendulkar. Under Ganguly, India reached the final of the 2003 ODI World Cup in South Africa, finishing as runners-up.Dhoni, meanwhile, led India to the 2011 ODI World Cup title on home soil, allowing Tendulkar to fulfil his long-standing dream of winning the tournament.Tendulkar praises Temba Bavuma's leadershipTendulkar also had words of appreciation for South Africa captain Temba Bavuma, praising the right-handed batter for leading his team from the front and producing impressive results."I truly admire Temba Bavuma’s spirit. He has led from the front and delivered some remarkable results for South Africa cricket. South Africa winning an ICC title is great for world cricket!"Bavuma's leadership has been backed by strong performances from the Proteas, including their 2-1 Test series victory over Australia in a three-match contest.The South African captain played a key role in the turnaround, scoring a career-best 179 in the second Test. In the series-deciding third Test at Newlands, off-spinner Simon Harmer delivered a match-winning performance, claiming 10 wickets in the game, including figures of 6/16 in the second innings.Harmer's efforts helped South Africa dismiss Australia for just 111 on the final day and seal the series 2-1.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma showed their fitness and fielding skills in India's first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday, producing two important dismissals.Kohli took a low catch at second slip to dismiss Nathan Smith in the 29th over off Anshul Kamboj, reducing New Zealand to 115/7. Smith went hard at a full delivery outside off stump, but managed only a thick edge. Kohli dived to his right and held on to the ball just inches above the ground. He followed it up with a 'Bow and Arrow' celebration.Earlier, Rohit helped India dismiss Daryl Mitchell in the 22nd over to claim New Zealand's fifth wicket. Mitchell nudged an Axar Patel delivery towards the leg side, prompting Rohit to rush in from mid-wicket. A moment of hesitation and confusion between the batters allowed Rohit to collect the ball and send in a quick underarm throw. KL Rahul completed the run-out with a swift collection behind the stumps.India captain Shubman Gill elected to field after winning the toss. The visitors went in with four specialist fast bowlers — Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh — who have a combined experience of 29 international matches. Mohammed Siraj was left out of the playing XI.Spin-bowling all-rounder Naman Dhir was preferred over seam-bowling all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy.FOLLOW LIVELineups:New Zealand: Tim Seifert, Will Young, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham, Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner (captain), Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy, Blair Tickner.India: Shubman Gill (captain), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, K.L. articles.title: A Hardik Pandya fan, Rohan Rajbhar slams maiden ton; dedicates milestone to mother after anchoring Rajasthan’s recovery alongside Mahipal Lomror
articles.summary: Playing only his fourth First-Class match, Rohan Rajbhar scored his maiden century, bringing up 140 off 263 balls with 11 fours and a six, as Rajasthan
articles.body: Playing only his fourth First-Class match, Rohan Rajbhar scored his maiden century, bringing up 140 off 263 balls with 11 fours and a six, as Rajasthan secured a lead of 222 runs against Himachal Pradesh on Day Two of their Group ‘D’ Ranji Trophy match in Dharamshala on Tuesday.Displaying rock-solid defence and executing exquisite strokes, Rohan anchored Rajasthan’s powerful comeback alongside Mahipal Lomror (97 off 190), with whom he stitched a crucial partnership of 209 runs.Upon reaching the landmark hundred, Rohan soaked in the applause, took off his helmet, and pulled out a piece of paper from his pocket to reveal a heartfelt message written on it: ‘Thank You Maa’. His marathon knock finally came to an end when he was stumped off an Abhishek Kumar delivery.For the 20-year-old, the milestone is the sweet fruit of an arduous journey born out of humble beginnings. His father, Vijay, who works as a POP (Plaster of Paris) contractor, always wanted his son to become a cricketer, so he sent Rohan to a cricket academy when he was just four years old. To make sure his son did not miss out on the opportunity, the father even borrowed money initially to cover the fees and buy his son the cricket gear.Growing up in a cramped one-room house where fans had to be switched off while his mother cooked in the shared space, Rohan learned early on what grit truly means. Reflecting on his special celebration, Rohan told TOI, “The message written on the paper was for my mother. She has never been able to watch my matches live at the stadium anywhere, so I knew she would be watching it on TV today. This hundred was for her.”He also credited senior pro Mahipal for steering him through tense moments. “Even on Day One when things weren’t going well, Mahipal bhai came up to me in the evening and kept encouraging me, telling me that I belong at this level and will do well. Out in the middle too, whenever my scoring slowed down or I played a reckless shot, he constantly guided and supported me.”That steely temperament draws deep inspiration from his idol, Hardik Pandya, whose peace symbol tattoo Rohan sports on his neck. The youngster’s admiration goes beyond cricket. He still vividly remembers when Hardik faced hostile booing across stadiums in India after he left Gujarat Titans and returned to Mumbai Indians as captain. “I had gone to see an IPL match at the SMS Stadium in 2024. I felt bad seeing a section of the spectators booing Hardik. I have great respect for him because of the way he has conducted himself in the face of criticism, and in life in general,” Rohan added.Meanwhile, the day belonged entirely to Rajasthan's remarkable redemption. Having been bundled out for a paltry 78 in their first innings, the visitors staged a phenomenal turnaround. After a disciplined first session where they lost just one wicket, the visitors pressed home their advantage with complete authority. It was only after tea that three wickets fell, including a heartbreaking end for Mahipal, who fell just three runs short of a well-deserved hundred after being caught by the wicketkeeper off medium-pacer Arpit Guleria.At stumps, Rajasthan reached a commanding 297/4, with captain Kartik Sharma and Vishal Harsh at the crease.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Literally belies logic’: Ex-cricketer questions Shubman Gill-led India's selection calls
articles.summary: Former India spinner Murali Kartik has questioned the team's selection strategy after Mohammed Siraj and Kuldeep Yadav were left out of the playing XI for
articles.body: Former India spinner Murali Kartik has questioned the team's selection strategy after Mohammed Siraj and Kuldeep Yadav were left out of the playing XI for the first ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday.India's combination for the series opener raised eyebrows, with Axar Patel and Naman Dhir featuring as the spin-bowling options. Kuldeep, meanwhile, continued to warm the bench after missing out throughout the preceding five-match T20I series.Siraj's absence was another decision that did not sit well with Kartik, who struggled to understand the reasoning behind leaving out established players while retaining others despite their recent performances.The former spinner also questioned the team's approach towards Nitish Kumar Reddy. He pointed out that India had picked the all-rounder for the match but did not include him in the playing XI, despite their stated intention of grooming him for a bigger role.Kartik was particularly critical of the bowling selections, referring to Gurnoor Brar's expensive outings and questioning why Mohammed Siraj had been dropped."Literally belies logic for me. I'm trying to figure out what, because what is it? Gurnoor has gone for 96 or 97 runs twice now," Kartik said on Cricbuzz."Aaqib Nabi did really well in Ranji Trophy cricket, and why are you getting rid of Mohammed Siraj from the playing XI? What wrong has he done? You are trying to groom Nitish Kumar Reddy as the next all-rounder, and you have picked him for only this game, but he is not there," he added.Kartik questions continued neglect of Kuldeep YadavKuldeep's prolonged absence from the playing XI was another major concern for Kartik. The wrist-spinner had been part of all three squad selections during the New Zealand tour but once again found himself on the sidelines for the opening ODI.Kartik also questioned whether the dimensions of Eden Park had any bearing on the decision to leave out the experienced spinner. He argued that New Zealand's grounds should not be compared with venues such as Melbourne or Adelaide when assessing the suitability of a spinner.Beyond the tactical considerations, the former India player highlighted the possible psychological impact of repeatedly being overlooked despite being part of the squad.He suggested that such uncertainty could leave a player wondering what more was required to secure a regular place in the team."Kuldeep Yadav, what does it have to do with the size of the boundary? New Zealand is not Melbourne or Adelaide. He is the common denominator; he is in all three squads. Whether you are a rhythm bowler or not, just from a mental perspective, you are always thinking about what needs to be done to find a regular place in all three teams," Kartik said.Meanwhile, New Zealand were bowled out for 185, with a late 39-run stand for the final wicket helping them avoid an even more disappointing total.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Arshdeep Singh scripts history, joins Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami in elite list as India bowl out New Zealand for 185
articles.summary: Arshdeep Singh joined Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami as the third Indian fast bowler to take a four-wicket haul in New Zealand, news agency ANI
articles.body: Arshdeep Singh joined Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami as the third Indian fast bowler to take a four-wicket haul in New Zealand, news agency ANI reported. He achieved the feat in the first ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday, finishing with figures of 4/70 from his 10 overs.Arshdeep's spell is the fourth-best by an Indian pacer in New Zealand. Srinath holds the top two positions with figures of 4/23 in Auckland in 2003 and 4/52 in Napier in 1995. Shami is third with 4/55 in Napier in 2014.Another wicket would have given Arshdeep his second five-wicket haul in ODIs and made him only the second Indian to take a five-for in New Zealand. Anil Kumble remains the only Indian to have achieved the feat, with figures of 5/33 in Wellington in 1994.Arshdeep has taken 12 wickets in five ODIs this year at an average of 23.08 and an economy rate of 6.08. His best figures during this period are 6/70.Speaking after the innings, Arshdeep said the conditions in New Zealand offered assistance to the bowlers and made it enjoyable to bowl."Loving the weather here and there is good purchase off the surface. After coming from the subcontinent, when you get some life in the wickets, it's always a pleasure to bowl here. And yeah, the wind is helping as well," he said.Explaining India's use of short-pitched deliveries, Arshdeep said the team looked to make the most of the assistance on offer from the surface."I felt like there was something in the wicket, so we were just trying to hit the seam hard and try to get purchase off the surface. And they were trying some shots of that length, so we got the wickets."The left-arm pacer said he was particularly disappointed to miss out on a fifth wicket."Favourite one would have been the fifth one, which I didn't get. So I am still searching for one," he said.Arshdeep also explained his dancing celebration after dismissing Kyle Jamieson, revealing that it was dedicated to his girlfriend, actor-model Samreen Kaur."That is for my girlfriend. We do these dance steps when we're out walking or something like that. Whenever the mood is a little low, we cheer each other up with that celebration. So this was for her," he added.Arshdeep's four-wicket haul helped India restrict New Zealand to 185 in the opening match of the five-ODI series at Eden Park. articles.title: Virat Kohli's 74, Arshdeep Singh's four-wicket haul guide India to victory against New Zealand in rain-hit ODI
articles.summary: Virat Kohli continued his remarkable run in the 50-over format with a commanding 74 as India defeated New Zealand by five wickets in a rain-affected first
articles.body: Virat Kohli continued his remarkable run in the 50-over format with a commanding 74 as India defeated New Zealand by five wickets in a rain-affected first ODI at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. The visitors chased down a revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.Kohli, who turns 38 on Thursday, brought up his 80th half-century in ODIs with another impressive display of batting in a run chase. The former India captain walked in after Rohit Sharma departed for a six-ball duck in the opening over and immediately took responsibility for rebuilding the innings.The experienced batter joined skipper Shubman Gill at the crease, and the pair stitched together a match-defining 113-run partnership for the second wicket. While Gill played the supporting role with a composed 37, Kohli took charge of the chase, finding boundaries regularly and keeping the required run rate under control.New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy picked up three wickets for 49 runs to briefly bring the hosts back into the contest. However, India had done enough damage through the Kohli-Gill partnership, and Naman Dhir eventually struck the winning boundary to seal the victory.India finished at 143/5 in 22.4 overs, securing a five-wicket victory and moving ahead in the series.India's pace attack dismantles New ZealandEarlier, India's young pace attack delivered an impressive performance to bowl New Zealand out for 185 in 40.2 overs after Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to field. Arshdeep Singh led the bowling effort with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj provided excellent support to keep the home side under constant pressure on a lively Eden Park surface.Arshdeep struck early to remove Will Young for nine before sending Henry Nicholls back to the pavilion for the same score. The left-arm pacer consistently used the bounce on offer and prevented the New Zealand top order from building momentum.Tim Seifert offered some resistance with a 38-run knock off 43 deliveries, which included three boundaries and two sixes. However, Gurnoor Brar eventually ended his stay with a short delivery as substitute fielder Ruturaj Gaikwad completed the catch.Brar continued to trouble the New Zealand batters with his pace and bounce. He also dismissed Tom Latham for three with a sharp return catch, leaving the hosts struggling at 84/4.Daryl Mitchell attempted to stabilise the innings alongside Glenn Phillips, but their partnership was broken following a run-out involving Rohit Sharma and KL Rahul. Mitchell departed for 28, while Phillips managed 30 off 51 deliveries before Arshdeep dismissed him.Anshul Kamboj was particularly impressive in the middle overs, keeping things tight with his disciplined line and length. The Haryana pacer dismissed New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner for four before removing Nathan Smith for one, finishing with figures of 2/22 in 10 overs, including two maidens.Kamboj conceded just 22 runs in his full quota, maintaining an economy rate of 2.20 and delivering 46 dot balls. His spell was among the most economical 10-over performances by an Indian fast bowler in recent years.New Zealand's lower order attempted to push the score towards 200, with Blair Tickner launching an aggressive counter-attack. The pacer smashed 34 off just 23 deliveries, including four sixes, but his efforts were not enough to take the hosts beyond 185.Arshdeep finished with 4/70, Brar claimed 3/44, while Kamboj returned 2/22 as India wrapped up the New Zealand innings in 40.2 overs.Rain interruptions disrupt India's chaseIndia's chase was interrupted by multiple rain delays, with the target eventually revised to 143 in 32 overs under the DLS method. The visitors suffered an early setback when Rohit Sharma was dismissed for a duck by Kyle Jamieson in the opening over. However, Gill and Kohli ensured there was no further damage during the initial phase of the chase.The victory gives India a 1-0 advantage in the five-match ODI series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: India captain Shubman Gill singled out Rohit Sharma's sharp run-out of Daryl Mitchell as the decisive moment in the team's five-wicket victory over New
articles.body: India captain Shubman Gill singled out Rohit Sharma's sharp run-out of Daryl Mitchell as the decisive moment in the team's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the rain-affected first ODI at Eden Park on Wednesday. Gill credited India's disciplined bowling and sharp fielding for restricting the hosts to 185, before Virat Kohli's commanding 74 helped the visitors chase down a revised target of 143.New Zealand appeared to be rebuilding their innings through a partnership between Mitchell and Glenn Phillips, but Rohit's alertness in the field brought an end to the stand and shifted the momentum in India's favour. Gill felt the dismissal was particularly important, considering how well the two batters had performed against India previously."I think we were very good with the bowling. And I think our fielding was also really good. That run out by Rohit bhai, I think changed the momentum of the game. I think it was really that partnership (Mitchell & Phillips), we saw that even in India - those two batted really well in India. And overall I think a very good team performance for us," Gill said after the match.India's bowlers ensured New Zealand never recovered from the setback, bowling them out for 185 in 40.2 overs. Arshdeep Singh led the attack with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar picked up three and Anshul Kamboj claimed two.Gill backs Kamboj and Brar after impressive bowling displaysGill was particularly pleased with the performances of Kamboj and Brar, who made excellent use of the conditions at Eden Park to trouble the New Zealand batters. Kamboj returned impressive figures of 2/22 in his 10 overs, while Brar finished with 3/44.The Indian skipper described Kamboj as a bowler suited to such conditions, highlighting his ability to generate movement with the new ball and remain effective with the older one. He also praised Brar's ability to extract additional bounce and trouble batters with his pace."I mean Anshul is the kind of a bowler, I think he's tailor-made for these kind of conditions, always nippy, trying to seam the ball. And good with the old ball. We felt when there's not much happening from the wicket, he (Brar) can create that extra bounce and with his pace and the way both of them bowled tonight was really magnificent to watch," he added.Gill explains how Kohli made rain-affected chase easierIndia's chase was far from straightforward, with two rain interruptions forcing changes to the target and the number of overs available. After the initial delay, the contest was reduced before another interruption brought the target down to 143 in 32 overs under the DLS method.Gill admitted that the changing conditions made batting difficult, particularly for players who had already settled at the crease. However, he credited Kohli's composed approach for making the chase considerably easier for India."It's never easy when you are set and then it rains and the wicket got a little bit quick, it got a little bit more nippy after the rain. So the target reduced. So we were just trying to play our normal cricket. And I think the way Virat bhai batted, it made things a lot more easy for us," Gill said.Kohli smashed 74 off 51 deliveries, registering his 80th ODI half-century, while Gill contributed 37. The duo added 113 runs for the second wicket to put India firmly in control before New Zealand's bowlers picked up a few late wickets.India eventually crossed the finish line at 143/5 in 22.4 overs, taking a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: James Anderson: Michael Atherton says Lancashire did not handle bowler's release badly - but should they have extended his contract?
articles.summary: Where could James Anderson end up next after release from boyhood club Lancashire? Sky Sports Cricket pundit Michael Atherton does not believe Old Trafford county handled Anderson's exit badly, saying director of cricket Paul Farbrace did not "hide behind the decision"
articles.body:
Anderson, 44, bagged 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 in the County Championship during a 2026 season in which Lancashire finished second bottom of Division Two under his captaincy.

Anderson was informed in a meeting with the Red Rose hierarchy that he would not be offered a new deal at a county he first represented in a first-class match in 2002, with new director of cricket Paul Farbrace wanting to build an attack for the future.

The decision came a little over two years after the fast bowler was retired by England against his wishes, with his final Test coming against West Indies at Lord's in July 2024.

Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast , alongside co-host in Nasser Hussain who had questioned the way Lancashire dispensed with Anderson's services , Atherton said: "I think you can argue about the merits of the decision as he was Lancashire's best bowler by a country mile last season.

"Forget age, young or old, if you are good enough, you are good enough, so you can make a perfectly good argument he should still be leading that Lancashire attack.

"Where I disagree with some of the comment elsewhere is that it has not been handled well, both by England and Lancashire.

"When somebody like Paul Farbrace comes in as director of cricket at Lancashire, or in England's case Rob Key, when they've decided to move on, how do you do that?

"In both instances, Anderson was told face-to-face. It wasn't done behind his back. Jimmy wasn't expecting [his Lancashire release], it took him by surprise, but it was face-to-face.

"They told him the rationale and then when the members meeting was held, I think Farbrace was abroad, but he dialled in and didn't hide behind the decision. He took full accountability for it.

"So I don't think you can say it's been handled badly.

"I thought England were right to move on at the stage that they did but Lancashire, if I'd have been in that position, I might have tried to get a season out of him next year."

Where next for Anderson if he carries on playing?

Speaking publicly for the first time since his departure from Old Trafford, on BBC podcast Tailenders , Anderson said he had not yet decided whether he would extend his county career.

He replied "wouldn't have thought so" when asked whether he could see himself turning out for Lancashire's fierce rivals Yorkshire.

If locality is high on the seamer's priority list then Durham could be an option.

However, the Chester-le-Street club, promoted to Division One at the end of the 2026 season, are well-stocked with pacers, especially if England keep overlooking Matthew Potts and Brydon Carse.

Leicestershire, Worcestershire and Derbyshire are also not an enormous trek from Manchester, so Anderson may perhaps be tempted to go to there, pass on his wisdom to younger bowlers, and try to help engineer promotion pushes from Division Two.

The early murmurings following Anderson's Lancashire release were that Division One clubs were interested in signing him, so maybe we should add Nottinghamshire , Warwickshire and Somerset to the list of possible destinations?

With Josh Tongue now an England regular, there may be space for Anderson in the Notts attack, while Somerset, still pursuing a long-awaited maiden County Championship title, could be eager to pair the veteran and Craig Overton as a new-ball duo.

If Anderson were to join Warwickshire, the 2026 Championship winners, he could bowl in tandem with former England colleague Chris Woakes and a player in Ethan Bamber who perhaps deserves to be in the conversation for international honours after 69 wickets at an average under 20 last term.

Many factors will play into Anderson's decision of whether to play on or not - who wants him, where he wants to go, how much money he is being offered - and if one of them is romance, then let's not rule a career-ending spell with Middlesex .

While Old Trafford was Anderson's home ground for a quarter of a century, he has enjoyed a love affair with the 'Home of Cricket' in Lord's, a venue where he bagged 123 wickets in 29 Tests during his England days, including seven five-fors.

Anderson's England career ended with an enforced retirement at Lord's. Maybe his domestic one could end on his own terms at the same place?

articles.title: WPL 2027 schedule announced: Vadodara, Mumbai to host fifth edition; RCB face MI in opener
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Wednesday announced the schedule for the fifth edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL),
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Wednesday announced the schedule for the fifth edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL), with Vadodara and Mumbai set to host the tournament from January 14 to February 7, 2027.The 22-match competition will feature five franchises, with 11 matches scheduled at each venue. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) will begin their title defence against former champions Mumbai Indians (MI) in the opening fixture at Vadodara on January 14.The fifth edition will begin with the Vadodara leg, which will run until January 24. The tournament will then move to Mumbai, with the Cricket Club of India's Brabourne Stadium hosting the remaining 11 matches from January 26.All matches, including the Playoffs, will begin at 7:30 PM IST.Brabourne Stadium to host Playoffs and finalThe league stage will continue in Mumbai until February 3, after which the tournament will enter the knockout phase.The Eliminator, featuring the teams finishing second and third in the league standings, will be played on February 5. The winner will advance to the final, where they will meet the table-toppers, who will earn direct qualification for the title clash.The final is scheduled for February 7 at the Brabourne Stadium, bringing the fifth edition of the WPL to a close.The five franchises will once again compete for the coveted title, with RCB entering the season as defending champions and looking to retain their crown.BCCI considering expansion of WPLThe schedule announcement comes days after BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia indicated that the Board could explore expanding the league beyond its existing five-team structure.The WPL has featured five franchises since its inaugural edition in 2023, but the BCCI is now considering ways to increase participation and further develop the competition."From next year, definitely we will have to do some brainstorming sessions to increase the number of teams as well as in other areas where we can improve," Saikia had said."Not only the players but so many other areas we are having involvement in, right from the coaches, selectors, etc, and various stakeholders are involved here," he added.Saikia also highlighted the league's contribution to women's cricket in India, describing it as one of the biggest franchise competitions in the sport."WPL is one of the big leagues in franchise cricket after IPL. We have come a long way in four years and ultimately we are now dominating women's cricket. WPL has contributed to the success of women's cricket in India," he said.Meanwhile, Sophie Molineux emerged as the costliest player at the recent auction, with UP Warriorz securing the services of the Australia captain for Rs 1.10 crore.WPL 2027 Full ScheduleVadodara legJanuary 14: Royal Challengers Bengaluru vs Mumbai IndiansJanuary 15: Gujarat Giants vs UP WarriorzJanuary 16: Delhi Capitals vs Royal Challengers BengaluruJanuary 17: UP Warriorz vs Mumbai IndiansJanuary 18: Gujarat Giants vs Delhi CapitalsJanuary 19: Royal Challengers Bengaluru vs UP WarriorzJanuary 20: Gujarat Giants vs Mumbai IndiansJanuary 21: UP Warriorz vs Delhi CapitalsJanuary 22: Gujarat Giants vs Royal Challengers BengaluruJanuary 23: Delhi Capitals vs Mumbai IndiansJanuary 24: UP Warriorz vs Gujarat GiantsMumbai legJanuary 26: Mumbai Indians vs Royal Challengers BengaluruJanuary 27: Delhi Capitals vs Gujarat GiantsJanuary 28: Mumbai Indians vs UP WarriorzJanuary 29: Royal Challengers Bengaluru vs Delhi CapitalsJanuary 30: Mumbai Indians vs Gujarat GiantsJanuary 31: UP Warriorz vs Royal Challengers BengaluruFebruary 1: Mumbai Indians vs Delhi CapitalsFebruary 2: Royal Challengers Bengaluru vs Gujarat GiantsFebruary 3: Delhi Capitals vs UP WarriorzPlayoffsFebruary 5: EliminatorFebruary 7: FinalGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Leicestershire's County Championship relegation confirmed as points deduction for 'poor' pitch upheld
articles.summary: Leicestershire join Hampshire in being relegated from Division One; Foxes argued that state of pitch for victory over Glamorgan had been due to shooting of Bollywood film days before fixture; Leicestershire finish 17 points behind third-bottom Essex in table as 19-point sanction stands
articles.body:
The Foxes were hit with a 27-point penalty, later cut to 19, after the surface at Grace Road was rated "poor" by the match referee following the win over Glamorgan in August.

Leicestershire, who argued the state of the pitch was due to the shooting of an unscheduled Bollywood film days before the Glamorgan fixture, had eight points from the original punishment of 27 reinstated but then appealed against the 19-point sanction.

However, the appeals panel supported the initial finding that the Midlanders had failed to act reasonably in preparing the wicket and, as a result, the club have slipped into the second tier of the Championship after finishing 17 points behind third-bottom Essex.

Had the appeal been successful and Leicestershire awarded all of their points back, Essex would have joined bottom team Hampshire in going down to Division Two.

A section of the County Championship's playing conditions stipulates that teams charged with producing a pitch rated as poor or below average earn zero points from that particular game.

Leicestershire earned 19 points from the 42-run win over Glamorgan - 16 for the victory itself and a further three bonus points.

Leicestershire have 'deep frustrations' over appeal process

Leicestershire chief executive Emma White said in a statement that the club "acknowledges and respects the conclusion of this process" but she also voiced "deep frustrations" that new evidence was not allowed to be presented.

White wrote: "As part of our appeal, we sought to introduce fresh expert evidence from one of the world's leading curators. We were not permitted to do so.

"We firmly believe this evidence would have made a significant difference to the outcome, and it is deeply frustrating that it could not be heard.

"From the outset, the club felt rushed and under considerable pressure throughout this process."

White added: "Pitch regulations are vitally important. They exist to ensure fairness across our competition, and we fully support them.

"However, the club believes there is an opportunity to bring greater clarity and consistency to pitch inspections, ratings and the processes that follow.

"We recognise the challenges involved in assessing pitches and would welcome further dialogue with the Cricket Regulator and the ECB to help counties better understand how decisions are reached."

The Foxes - who finished runners-up to Middlesex in this season's One Day Cup - were playing in Division One of the County Championship for the first time since 2003 having won promotion by winning the second tier in 2025.

White added: We are hugely disappointed by this outcome, but we will not allow it to define us.

"Our grounds team continues to have my full support, and I remain immensely proud of the work they do. Come pre-season, we will be ready to battle it out in Division Two, and to fight our way back.

Durham and Kent will take Leicestershire and Hampshire's spots in the top flight next season after finishing first and second respectively in Division Two in 2026.

articles.title: Unfazed by Emerging Teams Asia Cup snub, Priyansh Arya vows to keep pushing
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Priyansh Arya can hit sixes at will.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Priyansh Arya can hit sixes at will. With his brutal strokeplay, the Delhi batter can be as devastating as the best in the game and walk into any white-ball set-up. But he is also competing for a place in a generation that includes Abhishek Sharma, one of the world's best T20I batters, and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a bona fide superstar in the making.So, where does that leave Arya?The Delhi batter, who has been a regular for India A in white-ball cricket recently, has missed out on selection for the Tilak Varma-led squad for the upcoming Emerging Teams Asia Cup. India's openers will be Abhishek and Sooryavanshi, and Arya can consider himself unlucky.Priyansh Arya has a strike rate of 135.11 in List A cricket and 176.78 in T20s. In just four first-class matches, he has already shown promise, scoring a stunning 199. Priyansh, who plays for Punjab Kings, had the third-best strike rate in the 2026 Indian Premier League (IPL). He scored at a strike rate of 211.62. He was behind only Sooryavanshi and Finn Allen, while Abhishek Sharma was fourth.For a player who has consistently delivered with the bat, the omission raises a question: how does he break through when the competition is just as explosive and increasingly difficult to ignore?"I don't feel unlucky. Whatever I get, it is a lot. I am grateful, and it happens for everyone. You just have to keep pushing the door until it breaks," Arya told reporters on being overlooked for the Emerging Teams Asia Cup, to be held in Muscat from October 18-27.The Delhi batter, who scored a fine half-century in the innings, could prove to be a key player against Services on Day 4 of their ongoing Ranji Trophy match at the Air Force Complex Ground in Palam."The wicket is very good. In the first session, if there was a little moisture, the ball would seam a bit, and both teams took advantage of that. In the second session, the wicket gets a little hard, so the ball doesn't come on as well," he said."Tomorrow's first hour is very crucial. If we take five wickets, I think we can win outright. Our batting strength is very good. We can chase up to 300 runs. If we have enough time, it will be good for our team," he added.In Delhi's first match against Gujarat at the same venue, Arya fell one short of his double hundred. It was also his maiden first-class century."I didn't even know that I had scored 199! I was a little sad when I walked off the pitch, but it was part of the game. It's quite rare to score 199," recollected Arya.The southpaw said he was also helped by the words of Delhi coach Vijay Dahiya, a former India stumper. He said: "Coach motivates me a lot.""When we talk, it's not like we're playing a match just for three points. We always talk about going for an outright win. That is a good thing for both the team and individual growth."It will be a quick turnaround for the southpaw as he will be a force to reckon with in Delhi's pursuit of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, starting from November 14. Delhi's first match is against Jammu and Kashmir at the Holkar Stadium in Indore."There is less time for preparation, but we will see. Our team is very good in white-ball cricket, and if we win the trophy, that is the main focus. Many players are doing well in white-ball cricket, especially in the opening slot, where there is a lot of competition," said Arya.Arya also believes that transitioning between formats is largely about mindset. "Everything is based on our mindset. Whatever your mindset is, it helps us a lot, whether it is a red ball or a white ball," he said.The destructive batter also stressed the importance of red-ball cricket in a player's development. "If you see a good red-ball player, he can easily succeed in white-ball cricket. Red ball is very important."Having made his first-class debut last year, Arya believes the format has contributed to his growth as a cricketer. He, however, does not subscribe to the perception of players being labelled as red-ball or white-ball specialists. "I don't feel anything about the tag of being a 'white-ball' or 'red-ball' cricketer. It's just what people make up outside. It doesn't affect me at all," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Weather-hit Eden Gardens clash: Maharashtra put Bengal under pressure after reducing them to 76/4
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Weather continued to play spoilsport as Maharashtra enjoyed an upper hand in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ clash with Bengal at Eden Gardens
articles.body: KOLKATA: Weather continued to play spoilsport as Maharashtra enjoyed an upper hand in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ clash with Bengal at Eden Gardens here on Wednesday. The visitors will fancy their chances after reducing Bengal to 76/4 in the second innings, overall just one run ahead of Maharashtra’s first-innings total of 218, at stumps on Day III. Only 27.5 overs were bowled in the three hours and 16 minutes of play on the penultimate day which started after the whole first session was washed out due to rain.Maharashtra enjoyed a 75-run lead after their first innings ended in the fourth over of the morning, with 11 runs added to their overnight total of 207/9, when overnight unbeaten Pradeep Dadhe was trapped in front by Mohammed Shami for 27. Tanay Sanghvi remained unbeaten on 60 that came off 179 deliveries with the help of three boundaries and one six. Shami finished with 4/37 while Shahbaz Ahmed took 3/39.The Bengal second innings unfolded much like their first essay, with skipper Abhimanyu Easwaran the first to depart, chasing an away-going ball from Dadhe and being caught by wicketkeeper Saurabh Nawale in the fifth over of their innings. Sanghvi was in the thick of action when he bagged Sudip Gharami and Sudip Chatterjee in a gap of three deliveries to reduce Bengal to 25/3 just five overs later. Gharami played one on the rise and was caught at gully by Digvijay Patil for 12 while Chatterjee was trapped in front trying to play across the line without scoring.Opener Ankur Paul and Abishek Porel were involved in a 49-run fourth-wicket stand but did not look very convincing as Maharashtra skipper Prithvi Shaw set up an attacking field. The ploy did pay dividends as Paul was caught at silly point by Patil off left-arm spinner Hitesh Walunj for 32.Suraj Singh Jaiswal joined Porel as the duo was able to erase the deficit when bad light once again stopped play at tea after an extended second session of play.An outright win for Maharashtra will help them join Bengal at the top with 18 points while Bengal will look to save the match and return with one point, which will keep them as the sole leaders of the group.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
